## Working features

0.3.17 adds a bounded source card and study-family audit for the 2026 Lin PMV pilot, after review of the original publisher Methods/Results, Tables 1/2 and Figure 1. It separates 100 randomized/primary ITT participants from 91 protocol completers, the combined intervention from isolated protein or amino-acid effects, and the study prescription from delivered intake. Reported use of the approximate nitrogen equation is labelled **original-use context**, not validation of individual anabolic state or an optimal dose. Supplements and registry history remain unread. The library contains 65 sources and 18 selected relationship records; neither count is a unique-trial or participant total. See [Lin PMV sources and methods](./LIN-PMV-SOURCE-METHODS.md).

0.3.16 refines the existing PNI source map after direct comparison with the original English PubMed abstract: the published equation/units and the app's canonical-unit expression are algebraically equivalent. The role is explicitly **equation and units checked, abstract only**. Japanese full-text methods and contemporary ICU/ward clinical validity remain unreviewed. No PNI cutoff, clinical calculation, target or gate changed; no new trial or independent cohort was added. See [PNI original-equation methods](./PNI-SOURCE-METHODS.md). A separate draft local review-ledger tool in `research/` collects supplied review declarations against the frozen candidate/method files; it does not screen candidates automatically, approve a protocol or certify completed dual review. Its instructions and tests are in the local source package, outside the patient-data importer.

0.3.15 adds an expandable EN/TR **Sources for core calculations** panel and a compact `coreRuleProvenance` field on saved, synthetic and reimported records. It maps seven core output groups to canonical source IDs with explicit framework/context/unmapped roles. Local software policies are distinct from clinical source support. The map is not independent original-formula verification or a dose recommendation. Legacy research JSON remains accepted: incoming source maps are retained only in the historical `originalRecord`; current results and maps are rebuilt, current hashes are recorded, and confirmations reset. CSV adds one last JSON-valued column; previous columns stay in order. See [the implemented data dictionary](./DATA-DICTIONARY.md). No new literature retrieval, clinical equation or gate is introduced in this release.

- English default, Turkish selectable in the top bar. Locale preference alone persists; switching languages preserves inputs and user text.
- A four-step main workflow for assessment, laboratory verification, nutrition planning and research records. Colored summary cards, responsive navigation, contextual details and reduced-motion support keep the main task visible.
- BMI, weight change, verified NLR/PNI and approximate nitrogen balance under collection/intake constraints. These do not establish a definitive anabolic/catabolic diagnosis.
- Separate GLIM/ESPEN/AND-ASPEN candidate findings, NRS 2002 risk and EWGSOP2 functional assessment. Missing data are explicit. FFMI is distinct from appendicular mass.
- Dysphagia records: EAT-10 total, FOIS, separate IDDSI food/fluid levels, assessment/source/date and safety flags. Unsafe swallowing/alertness blocks an oral draft.
- Reviewed chronic history and IBD type/phase, renal conflicts, absorption and fluid context. Intestinal failure, high-output losses or obstruction disable the general draft.
- Explicit urea/BUN units, paired-date UCR and local CRP reference ratio. Verified adult ICU SOFA-2 components are calculated; SAPS II is a clinician-entered, independently calculated total. Organ scores are not inflammation grades or nutrition-dose rules.
- Physician-set energy/protein targets, other intake and verified product composition determine formula volume, delivered protein/energy, remaining deficits and formula-derived free water. No automatic amino acid or SCFA dose.
- Four evidence comparisons: ICU protein, refeeding approaches, glutamine, and leucine/BCAA/HMB. Population, exposure, uncertainty and source access accompany optional physician choice/reasoning. Imported or changed assessments require renewed review.
- 65 source records, including 25 non-held records labelled 2026 and one additional quality-hold record. Year does not establish study quality; publication issue and online dates are distinguished when verified.
- CSV/JSON laboratory import with unit/date checks; local PDF/TXT selectable-text reading and manual verification. No OCR for scanned images.
- Session research records, JSON/CSV export, original-record preservation on reimport and printable selected-language assessment trace with clinical-module summaries.

## Nutrition delivery follow-up (0.3.0)

### 0.3.1 date and interpretation repair

Laboratory indices require a real assessment date. Nitrogen balance requires its own UUN date matching the written collection-end day and not after assessment. Missing UUN date suppresses its estimate; old files receive no invented date. UUN imports retain source date; date edits clear old UUN values/provenance and manual edits replace provenance. Case/date changes reset confirmations. Kidney-history and major intestinal-loss contradictions suppress nitrogen interpretation both in the main view and follow-up. Energy/protein delivery comparisons remain descriptive and are not erased by loss of an eligible nitrogen estimate. See METABOLIC-METHODS-AND-VALIDATION.md for methods, source access, and staged clinical-validation requirements.

A verified actual-energy/protein ledger now compares complete 24-hour delivery with an unchanged physician prescription. Research records show separate delivery and matched nitrogen-balance plots. Case, admission, setting, phase and plan version define the comparison. Duplicate/overlapping records are excluded together until a revision is explicitly selected; missing periods are not zero-filled. JSON preserves comparison selection and imported provenance; CSV includes record IDs, selected/included flags, exclusions and summary. Imported observations require renewed verification. See FOLLOW-UP-METHODS.md.

## Scope and data

Renal disease/KRT, high or unknown refeeding risk, instability, unreliable weight and other core exclusions keep the generic draft disabled. Added swallowing and disease-context gates also apply. A physician confirmation cannot bypass these gates. Evidence choices never modify numerical targets automatically.

Current raw patient drafts and immutable saved assessments are written to local SQLite under `nutrition/data/`. Wait for **Saved on this computer** before closing or changing cases. Use a study code and the saved-patients panel to reopen earlier drafts/history. Manual and daily backups stay local; software ZIPs exclude patient data and QA sandboxes. This is a single Windows account/workstation workflow; shared LAN access, role-based login, encryption at rest and an immutable institutional audit service are not implemented. See [Local patient records](./LOCAL-PATIENT-RECORDS.md). A physiological/optimal-dose study retains its separate institutional design and validation requirements.

JSON/CSV retain canonical original clinical text and bilingual clinical-module values; the printable UI follows the selected language. Downloadable methods are labelled by language. Regenerated EN/TR PDF pagination remains pending in the current acceptance cycle.

## Run locally

Use the complete desktop edition folder. Double-click its **`START.cmd`** to start the owned background server and open **http://127.0.0.1:4188**. Repeated starts reuse that server. Use **`STOP.cmd`** when finished; it stops only the server belonging to this folder. The root `LOCAL-USAGE.md` is the current start/stop and storage guide. No Sites service, global Node/npm installation or internet download is required to start the bundled local app.

The local Research records page supplies synthetic input, replay report and method downloads. Older Site references describe the historical hosted edition, not the current runtime or an upload destination. For the separate synthetic analysis demonstration, start PowerShell in the canonical root:

```powershell
& .\runtime\node.exe .\work\nutriklinik\analysis\run.mjs --input .\work\nutriklinik\analysis\fixtures\synthetic-agreement.json --output .\work\synthetic-analysis-report.json
```

This is an external synthetic schema, not a clinical laboratory/research JSON import; no real patient analysis was performed. Application drafts and saved assessments use the local SQLite store described above; exports and a separate backup copy remain useful recovery tools. External article links and new literature research require internet; clinical computation and local file reading do not. PDF.js and its license are bundled in `work/nutriklinik/dist/vendor/`.

For development verification, from the canonical root:

```powershell
Set-Location .\work\nutriklinik
& ..\..\runtime\node.exe --test
```

After source changes, the local maintainer can run `& ..\..\runtime\node.exe release.mjs` from that application directory to refresh hashes and the source catalog. This is a local build operation, not publication or remote deployment. Engine and assessment SHA-256 values are in `dist/build-info.mjs` and `dist/release-info.json`; they support reproducibility, not clinical certification.

## Türkçe kısa açıklama

Varsayılan dil İngilizce; üstten Türkçe seçilir. Ana amaç malnütrisyon/metabolik değerlendirme ve hekim hedeflerine göre mama taslağıdır. Ek kriterler, disfaji ve kronik hastalık bağlamı bu akışı destekler. Bütirat notu yalnız seçilmiş İBH bağlamında ikincil kanıttır. SOFA-2 hesaplanır; SAPS II bu sürümde klinisyenin hesapladığı toplam olarak kaydedilir. Kesin anabolik/katabolik tanı ve otomatik optimal doz iddiası yoktur. Araştırma protokolü ve veri sözlüğü çalışma taslağıdır. NutriClinic klinik kararı destekler, yerine geçmez.
